text.text: Run the salon from one page. Clients, the service menu and payments are linked, and every appointment is a row with a stylist. Stylists find their chair under Mine. The service menu shows how many regulars book each service.
Everything on the menu, its price, time and how many regulars book it.
Clients with their usual service, visit history and spend.
The salon book: who is in the chair, with which stylist, and when.
Charges, failed cards and refunds, tied to each client.
The best time to book the next visit is before the client leaves the chair.
Offer the next appointment at the end of every service.
Write the date on the appointment card and enter it right away.
Send a reminder two days before.
If the client declines, add a follow-up in six weeks.
Keep a short list of clients who want any cancellation. Call them first when a slot opens.
A recorded formula is the difference between a match and a mistake.
Write the brand, shade, developer and ratio on the appointment note.
Note processing time and the result.
Take a photo with the client permission.
Always do a patch test for new color clients or any new product. Record the date and result.
Retail is high-margin. Keep it tidy and counted.
Move slow items to the front.
Till counted and the book updated for tomorrow.
